questions.question: Does the brittleness of the CrMoNbWV HEA at room temperature originate primarily from the incoherent hexagonal oxides or the Laves phases, given that both are present and localized at grain boundaries?
questions.rationale: The paper identifies two potential sources of brittleness: incoherent oxides and brittle Laves phases localized at grain boundaries. Identifying the dominant contributor allows for targeted microstructural control (e.g., oxide suppression vs. Laves phase reduction) to improve toughness.
questions.decision_use: Prioritize process adjustments to eliminate the specific phase causing the most significant crack propagation.
answer_requirements: Perform in-situ tensile testing with optical microscopy to track crack initiation sites relative to oxide vs. Laves phase distribution
Calculate fracture toughness contributions of each phase via nanoindentation mapping
evidence_spans: In addition, the precipitated oxides have a hexagonal lattice that is incoherent to the CrMoNbWV HEA BCC-matrix. It leads to the high strength of the material but simultaneously to the brittleness as well.
These phases were brittle at room temperature, and their localization promoted a crack initiation and propagation along the grain boundaries resulting in a decrease of the HEA plasticity.
